### The God Who Sees You
Author: Jo Saxton
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement/encouragement-for-today-august-23-2021.html
Passage: Genesis 16:13
Points:
- In seasons of exhausting crisis and heartbreak, God invites honest tears rather than forced strength.
- Hagar was used and discarded amid broken family dynamics, yet God sought her out in the desert.
- Naming God El Roi reminds us that He intimately sees our hidden distress and personal pain.
- God tracks every season of our lives and remains faithful to redeem our stories.

### What Hagar and Genesis 16 Teach Us About 'The God Who Sees'
Author: Jeff Mingee
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/god-seeing-not-scrolling/
Passage: Genesis 16:13
Points:
- Unlike the distracted, passive gaze of social media culture, God's attention is focused, intentional, and constant.
- Abram and Sarai used Hagar for their own ends without truly seeing or valuing her as a person.
- In the wilderness, the mistreated runaway became the only person in Scripture to confer a name upon God.
- The Lord does not simply observe from a distance; He stays near and cares with a Savior's heart.

### The LORD Has Listened
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/lord-has-listened
Passage: Genesis 16:11-12
Points:
- God met Hagar in her distress and instructed her to name her son Ishmael, meaning "God hears."
- The child's name stood as a lifelong testimony that the Lord actively attended to Hagar in her affliction.
- The prophecy concerning Ishmael reveals the long-lasting conflict that follows attempts to fulfill God's promises through human schemes.
- Even though Ishmael was outside the covenant line, believers are called to remember that God's gospel grace extends to all nations.

### El Roi: The God Who Sees Us
Author: Emma Danzey
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/the-one-who-sees-us-the-crosswalk-devotional.html
Passage: Genesis 16:13
Points:
- Many people navigate seasons of deep isolation where they feel completely overlooked by those around them.
- Hagar was subjected to painful mistreatment, yet the angel of the Lord met her in the wilderness with words of hope.
- God revealed Himself as El Roi, showing that no person in pain is truly forgotten or invisible to Him.
- Believers can counter lies of unworthiness by remembering Christ's faithful presence and persistent love.
